Friday, September 18, 2026 · 10:00 AM
St. Mark’s Church
450 Oak Avenue, Riverside

Robert James Carter was born on June 12, 1948, in Riverside, the eldest of three sons of Harold and Mary Carter. He grew up fishing the river with his father and fixing anything with an engine, and he graduated from Riverside High School in 1966.
Robert served four years in the United States Navy before starting a thirty-eight-year career with the county water department, where he was known for his steady hands and his terrible jokes. In 1971 he married the love of his life, Linda Reyes, and together they raised three children in the house on Oak Avenue.
He coached Little League for twenty summers, sang bass in the church choir and never met a stranger. He was happiest in his workshop, on the lake at sunrise or at the head of a crowded Sunday table, telling the same stories everyone loved to hear again.
He was preceded in death by his parents and his brother, Edward. He is survived by his wife of fifty-five years, Linda; his children, Thomas Carter (Anna), Karen Wallace (Mike) and William Carter; seven grandchildren; his brother, George; and many friends. His faith, his humor and his generous heart will be missed by all who knew him.
The family thanks you for joining us today.

William Henry Brooks was born on October 3, 1952, in Cedar Ridge, the youngest of four children of Henry and Alice Brooks. He grew up on the lake, learned to swing a hammer in his father’s shop before he could ride a bike, and graduated from Cedar Ridge High School in 1970.
Bill spent forty-two years as a carpenter and builder, and there is hardly a street in town without a porch, a barn or a set of kitchen cabinets that he built with his own hands. In 1975 he married Carol Sullivan, and together they raised three children in the house on Lakeshore Drive that he built himself.
He loved a cold morning in a duck blind, a long day on the water and a Saturday afternoon of football with the grandkids. He kept the church roof tight for thirty years, never charged a neighbor for a repair and could not pass a broken fence without stopping to fix it.
He was preceded in death by his parents and his sister, Joan. He is survived by his wife of fifty-one years, Carol; his children, Daniel Brooks (Sarah), Emily Nolan (Charlie) and Matthew Brooks; eight grandchildren; his brothers, Jim and Ray; and many friends. His steady hands, his quiet humor and his generous heart will be missed by all who knew him.
The family thanks you for joining us today.
